usual_baseline: Scoring systems almost never used: 0–2.6%. Imaging ranges from 61.3% to 92.5%. Surgery within 24 hours of decision 73.4–89.1%, delays mostly theatre capacity. Negative appendicectomy 4.2–15.4%. Postoperative antibiotics given to 67.2–92.1%, with choice and duration varying widely.
fix_that_works: Only one closed loop. Time to diagnosis fell from 16.8 to 8.27 hours, diagnosis to surgery from 28.1 to 20.54 hours, drains from 44% to 31%, postoperative antibiotics from 92.1% to 75.6% and complications from 17.8% to 3.3% [2853]. The intervention is not described.
fix_that_fails: Scoring system use stayed low, 0% to 3.3% [2853]. No other re-audit reported; an educational push on scoring was only proposed [2255].
consultant_advice: A broad 'management of appendicitis' audit mostly re-finds low score use and theatre delays. Pick one measurable item and close the loop. Most useful: why CT- or ultrasound-diagnosed cases are histologically negative (about 25% in one unit [2839]) and whether postoperative antibiotics are really needed.
